deep.reconstruction:
This page is not written by Riemann. It is part of a letter from Karl Hattendorff to the editor of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke, almost certainly Heinrich Weber (first edition 1876). Hattendorff had edited Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Ueber die Flaeche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Goettingen 13, 1867). The letter discusses revisions for its reprint. The reference to Schwarz's 'Miscellen' (Schwarz, 'Miscellen aus dem Gebiete der Minimalflaechen', Crelle 80, 1875) dates the letter to about 1875-76.

Content, paragraph by paragraph:

(1) Enneper. Hattendorff has not yet been able to look at Enneper's papers in vol. 9 of Schloemilch's Zeitschrift fuer Mathematik und Physik (1864) or in the Goettinger Nachrichten for 1866. From memory, he says Enneper did not start from a prescribed boundary in order to find the minimal surface. Instead Enneper generated his 'cyclic surfaces' (surfaces swept out by a moving circle) and remarked in passing that such a surface satisfies the PDE of minimal surfaces.

(2) Addendum to the introduction. The addendum at the end of the introduction was meant to cite Weierstrass's investigations (Monatsberichte Berlin 1866), which Hattendorff did not know at the time of the first printing. He hopes Schwarz is thereby also given his due. Schwarz's 'Miscellen' are better left unmentioned.

(3) Error in the memoir. Hattendorff admits an error on p. 14 of the 1867 edition: the assumption dv/dt = phi'(t)/sqrt(chi(t)). He explains how it arose:
- Riemann had struck out three examples (p. 31 top) in the manuscript.
- The passage immediately before them was left standing, and it speaks only of the points c.
- Since the function k_1 stays continuous at the other points, Hattendorff skipped recomputing (1/k) d^2k/dv^2 there.

The next page gives the fix: keep only the substitution dv/dt = 1/sqrt(phi(t) chi(t)), with which the investigation can be carried through in full generality.

In modern terms (my gloss): in Riemann's treatment of minimal surfaces bounded by straight lines, auxiliary functions k satisfy a second-order linear ODE. The coefficient (1/k) d^2k/dv^2 must be regular except at prescribed singular points. Changing the variable from t to v changes this coefficient by a Schwarzian-type term. With dv/dt = 1/sqrt(phi chi), we have d/dv = sqrt(phi chi) d/dt (my step). Hence

 k_vv = phi chi k_tt + (1/2)(phi chi)' k_t.

The singular behaviour of this expression at the zeros of phi and chi must be checked, and that is the check Hattendorff omitted. No derivation is actually carried out on this page.
errors: Not an error on the page itself: the page reports an editorial error in the 1867 edition (p. 14), namely the substitution dv/dt = phi'(t)/sqrt(chi(t)), which Hattendorff concedes and proposes to replace by dv/dt = 1/sqrt(phi(t) chi(t)).

Hattendorff's description of Enneper is explicitly from memory. Enneper's 1864 paper does study minimal surfaces generated by circles (cyclic minimal surfaces, including Riemann's own family), so the characterisation is roughly fair.

deep.surprise_reason: This is editorial correspondence by Hattendorff (about 1875-76) about the reprint of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir, not Riemann's own mathematics. It contains historiographical remarks and the acknowledgment of a known editorial slip, consistent with what is known of the Werke's editorial history.

transcription_corrections: Author attribution: the page is by Karl Hattendorff (letter to the Werke editor, presumably H. Weber), not by Riemann.
'Miscellen' is clearly written in quotation marks („Miscellen“); the [?] can be removed. It refers to Schwarz's 'Miscellen aus dem Gebiete der Minimalflaechen' (1875).
Transcription otherwise matches the image: 'Irrtum', 'S. 14.', 'S. 31. oben', 'M.S.'; the formula reads dv/dt = phi'(t)/sqrt(chi(t)).
